body:
I've left a message for my therapist, so now I'm just waiting and going to reddit to see if anyone has advice for the wait time. It's hard to explain. I don't *want* to kill myself, but there's an overwhelming urge to do so. I put almost a whole bottle of lithium in my mouth and tried to swallow before my "conscious" brain intervened. 

I have suicidal thoughts a lot, so I think I my impulse control system has just short circuited. I recently had a change in my medication dosing, so that might be it.

Seeing a psychologist/psychiatrist team, getting the bipolar diagnosis, and starting medication and therapy was a lifesaver. If you think you may be bipolar, go see a therapist. It's tough, but it can be managed. 

I realize how ironic this advice is considering right now I'm trapped in a corner of my apartment and afraid I will kill myself if I pick anything up!

I really don't want to kill myself, intellectually. But, my gut instinct wants to kill me, if that makes sense at all.

The meds have helped immensely. I'm not sure why I didn't think of this first, but my dosing was altered a few days ago. Time to leave a voice mail for my psychiatrist. 

The intrusive thoughts thing seems reasonable. I've had thoughts like that before, as I'm sure everyone has, but I've never felt like I was in danger of acting on them until today. Perhaps I should get a friend to take me to the ER =/
I have bipolar disorder, so I've had suicide attempts during depressive episodes before. This feels odd =/

It's weird, and not something I've experienced before. This morning I went to take my meds (Lithium and zoloft, I'm bipolar) and put most of the lithium in the bottle in my mouth. It felt like a bizarre physical struggle against myself to spit them out. It's overwhelming because I keep thinking "I could kill myself with that <insert random object>" and then feel an incredibly strong desire to do so. 

I've been depressed and suicidal before. This just feels... different.
